preamble: Seven theme clues require 9 25 20 inserted to reach the solution to be entered in the grid

clue.text: Remove clothing to loud music

explanation.surface: A striptease performed to a heavy soundtrack.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme clue: per the preamble, a three-piece run of the alphabet goes into the wordplay's word, here in front, to make the grid entry. 'Clothing' looks like the garments themselves; it is a priest's frock.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally taking away a priest's frock, the word means expelling a cleric from holy orders.

clue.text: F-stop used on images, first of Turkish gents

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is the singular title, though effendi can serve as its own plural

parts.note: the letter F written out as a word

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

explanation.surface: A photographer's note on aperture settings for pictures of Turkish gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'F-stop' looks like one camera term, but the hyphen splits it: the letter F spelt out, then a word for stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi is an old Ottoman courtesy title for a man of standing, roughly sir or master.

clue.text: Rectify a dry condition there all round

definitions.text: Rectify a dry condition there all round

indicators.note: spread all round, the letters are scattered and land in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Advice for fixing a parched patch of ground by watering it everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the mixed letters of the two fragments describe putting water back.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore moisture lost through drying out is exactly to cure a parched state.

clue.text: Present debate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bestow, as an honour or degree
second meaning: to discuss or consult together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Present debate' reads as a noun phrase about a current argument; both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both formally granting an award and holding a discussion with colleagues.

clue.text: Play about with complete collection

indicators.note: knocked about, the letters are moved around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A child fiddling with a full set of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme clue: the wordplay gives PALY, and the run NOP, three letters in alphabetical order, goes into its middle for the grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a full suit of armour, the word now means an impressive, extensive array of things.

clue.text: Float around in sea, stormy recently

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is enclosed by it
turned around, the word's letters are moved out of order
stormy conditions churn things up, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Something has been drifting about on a rough sea lately.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: the jumbled first word goes inside the jumbled sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning lately or in the recent past.

clue.text: Boy who goes before Italian pope

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet this word comes just before Papa, the Italian for pope

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests papal succession, but Papa is the Italian for pope and also the NATO code word for P; the code word for O precedes it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common male given name and the radio alphabet's word for the letter O.

clue.text: Experimental clothing worn a lot

indicators.note: something worn is battered out of its original shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Avant-garde garments that get plenty of wear.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme clue: the wordplay gives LOAT, and ABC, the alphabet's opening run, goes inside to make the grid entry. 'Experimental' sounds like avant-garde fashion but means for experiments.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientists wear this white overall while running tests, so it is the garment of experimentation.

clue.text: Arranging characters of pleasing habit in new fashion

indicators.note: something made in a new fashion is remade in a different form

explanation.surface: Describes people of agreeable manners going about things in a modern style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' sounds like people with a pleasing habit, but here it means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting letters or words into A-to-Z sequence is sorting written symbols by order.

clue.text: Two articles on a type of coat

wordplay.note: the indefinite article in both its forms, one then the other

explanation.surface: A newspaper running two features about one kind of coat.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme clue: per the preamble, three consecutive alphabet letters are slotted between the two articles to make the grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin coat with the fleece inside, popular in the 1960s and 70s, takes its name from Afghanistan.

clue.text: African princes uncoil lazily — obese, even

indicators.note: done lazily, things end up sprawled any which way, out of order
even positions are the second, fourth and so on, so only those are kept

explanation.surface: Pampered African royals lounging and stretching out, a bit overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: The lion is king of the beasts, so its young are playfully called princes.
explanation.definitionFit: If the lion is the king of the jungle, its offspring are the heirs to that throne.

clue.text: Leading person of fashion, looking back

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the order runs right to left
what leads comes at the front, so the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A trendsetter glancing over their shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'person of' do double duty, building the wordplay and also sitting inside the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a man excessively concerned with clothes and appearance, a slave to style.

clue.text: Where doctor would go to dig beneath the surface in state of anxiety

parts.note: these two letters occupy the spot the abbreviation DR would fill
to dredge is to dig up a riverbed; remove DR and this is what remains

explanation.surface: A surgeon going deeper into a patient while feeling nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: To dig beneath the surface is to DREDGE; DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor. Put ON where DR would go in that word and you have the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervy, tense or jumpy is an everyday idiom for worry and unease.

clue.text: Gangster grabs every other top layer, making one cross

indicators.note: to grab something is to hold it inside your grip

parts.note: a hood, short for hoodlum, is a gangster

indicators.note: taking every other one means keeping one, skipping one, keeping the next

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A mobster snatching a layer off the top and getting angry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for the gangster's mood, but it is a noun: one particular cross. HOLYROOD is also the Edinburgh palace and Scottish Parliament site.
explanation.definitionFit: Rood is an old word for crucifix, and this name refers to the true Cross of Christ.

clue.text: Boatman's modest clothing

wordplay.note: an AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: The setter, Boatman, owning up to his decent attire.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives only AB; this is a theme clue, so three alphabetically consecutive letters go in, here at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: This headscarf is worn by many Muslim women for reasons of modesty in dress.

clue.text: Resumes obscure, useless legal measures

indicators.note: the word is read as 'use-less': lacking 'use', so those three letters come out

explanation.surface: A complaint that some legal rulings are arcane and achieve nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resumes' looks like a verb (starts again) but is the plural noun, summaries; 'useless' tells you to drop U, S, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary of a paper or report placed at its head is called by this name.

clue.text: Boatman may be found here initially?

definitions.text: Boatman may be found here initially?

parts.note: surface reading: a sailor's natural place is in the middle of the vessel
setter's reading: Boatman, the setter, has hidden runs of consecutive letters in the middle of the theme words

explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is this puzzle's setter, so the clue is about him as well as any oarsman; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in the middle part of a vessel, where a sailor might be stationed.

clue.text: Pi and nu: letters sent back, not stopping on in going away

indicators.note: letters sent back are returned in the opposite order
whatever goes away leaves, so those letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Reads like a maths or Greek-alphabet note about letters being returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi and nu look like a pair of Greek letters, but pi is the definition: British slang short for pious. Take ON and IN out of CONTINUOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pi is informal British for sanctimonious, and an oily, smugly pious manner is this.

clue.text: Every other neat clue?

parts.note: setter's reading: split the answer as 'alter' plus an anagram of 'neat', and it is itself a tiny clue whose answer is neat

explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as two words is a miniature clue: an instruction to rearrange four letters, which come back as 'neat'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means occurring on every second occasion, skipping one each time.

clue.text: See 28
See 25
Twice this might express doubt about clothing

wordplay.note: 'Come, come!' said in disbelief is a way of doubting what you hear

explanation.surface: A doubtful reaction, repeated, to someone's outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme clue: the wordplay gives COME, and the alphabetical run STU goes into its middle for the grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of garments, especially for a play or fancy dress, is a general word for dress.

clue.text: Italian sauce used around start of Ramadan fast

indicators.note: wrapped around something, one item encloses another
the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone eating Italian food just as the Ramadan fast begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' sits next to Ramadan as if it were the fasting period, but it means quick.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical tempo marking means very quick, and it is also used for 'quickly'.

clue.text: Acts of government constraining extremes of unrest by society

indicators.note: to constrain is to hold in, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: the state is the governing body

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Laws passed by a regime that clamp down on rioting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts of government' looks like the definition as a whole, but 'of government' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws passed by a legislature are formally known as Acts, written statutory rules.

clue.text: Quality to suit aristocrat, backed by independent European Commission in article

indicators.note: to be in something is to be enclosed by it
something backed has been moved backwards, so it reads in the other direction

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A noble's tailoring standards, set alongside a Brussels body's rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like a verb (to please), but it is the garment; this answer is a quality a suit can have.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit made of jacket, trousers and waistcoat is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Struggle against Daesh taken on by others

indicators.note: taken on board by something, an item sits inside it

parts.note: Daesh is another name for the terror group Islamic State, IS

explanation.surface: A coalition of nations joining the fight against the jihadist group.
explanation.walkthrough: Daesh is the Arabic-derived name for so-called Islamic State, abbreviated IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight back against or oppose something is a plain synonym for withstanding it.

clue.text: Part of the Arctic environment

indicators.note: a part of something is a piece lying within it

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A geography lesson on what makes up the polar north.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the hiding place and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water covers much of the polar north, so it is a defining feature there.

clue.text: A lover fears them: her last tender quivering embraces, sweetheart

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one piece wraps round another
quivering means shaking, and shaken letters fall in a new order

parts.note: jo is a Scots word for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A dramatic picture of a woman trembling as she hugs her beloved for the last time.
explanation.walkthrough: JO is a Scots word for a sweetheart, familiar from Burns's 'John Anderson, my jo'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are notes ending a romance, and anyone in love dreads receiving one.

clue.text: Novices going the wrong way by mistake

indicators.note: travelling the wrong way means heading backwards, right to left

explanation.surface: Beginners drivers heading down a one-way street in error.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests learners lost on the road; the novices are school pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A small blunder or error is called this in casual speech.

clue.text: Report of Treasury for Halfwits is libel

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: a purse holds money, a treasury; asses are halfwits

explanation.surface: Reads like an insulting newspaper headline about a finance ministry run by fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like an official document, but it signals sound; a donkey's wallet, said quickly, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to damage someone's good name with false or harmful claims.

clue.text: Heartlessly pursued type of fabric

indicators.note: without a heart, a word loses its central letter

parts.note: to woo is to pursue romantically

explanation.surface: A suitor chasing someone coldly, or a dull note on cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme clue: the wordplay gives WOED, and the alphabetical run RST goes into its middle for the grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This smooth woollen yarn and cloth, named after a Norfolk village, is used for suits.
